text: At what training step do the distance, energy and force probes first beat their controls, and does that coincide with the drop in val_mse_ratio below 0.1 around steps 1000-1750? This needs probes at intermediate checkpoints.

Is the force probe signal (R2 0.728 vs control 0.526) actually a physical-force representation, or a proxy for accel_step = (2*pi/N)^2 * a^3 / ((1+m2) * r^2)? Probing force and accel_step together at all layers would show which one the model encodes.

Is the velocity probe a meaningful test? The random-init control already reaches R2 0.878, likely because relative velocity is almost a linear difference of consecutive input positions, which caps the possible margin. Would probing velocity at a later token position, or after removing the input-embedding contribution, separate learned structure from input leakage?

Does the force probe keep any R2 above control after accel_step is regressed out of the target (and vice versa)? Force is best at layer 4 with margin 0.222, while accel_step is best at layer 1 with R2 0.917 and margin 0.175, and the two targets are collinear through 1/r^2.

Across the E6 scaling grid, which of force and accel_step has the larger margin over its random control, and does that change with scale? In this cell (L=2, d=32, N=1000) force leads, 0.298 vs 0.204, while in an earlier model accel_step had the higher raw R2.

Why does the random-init control reach R2 0.584 on accel_step but only 0.014 on distance? Is accel_step's control R2 driven by the a^3 orbit-scale factor that is visible in the raw input coordinates, which would cap how much the accel_step margin can measure?

Does widening the mass ratio range to [0.01, 1] change val_mse_ratio or the random-control R2 for force? If the control R2 for force drops sharply, part of the earlier force margin may have come from the narrow m2 range making force track 1/r^2 (and therefore distance) almost exactly.
Does a smaller 4-layer d_model=64 model show the same accel_step-over-force pattern as the d_model=128 run (run-20261011-193740-63f2), or does the ranking of the two targets depend on model width?

Why does the force margin keep growing through training (0.107 to 0.223 in seed 2, 0.092 to 0.230 in seed 3) while the accel_step margin levels off at about 0.17-0.20 after step 750? Does the late force gain survive regressing accel_step and distance out of the force target?

Between step 0 and step 250, do the accel_step and distance margins cross 0.1 before, together with, or after val_mse_ratio first drops below 1? Checkpoints every 25 steps in a 4-layer d_model=64 model would show this.

If transfer fails specifically on high-eccentricity systems, is that because 1/r^2 is outside the training range at pericentre (an extrapolation failure of the learned function) or because the model uses a near-circular shortcut? Comparing the size of the error against r at each snapshot would tell these apart.
Does the accel_step random-control R2 (0.71-0.75) also stay high on OOD eval sets? If it does, the a^3 orbit-scale factor visible in the raw inputs is the likely cause, not anything learned.

Is m2 itself linearly decodable from the residual stream above its random control when m2 ranges over [0.01, 1]? If it is not, the force margin (0.235-0.243) must come from the 1/r^2 or distance part of force rather than an m2-weighted force.

If probe success is measured as headroom-normalized margin, (R2-control)/(1-control), instead of raw margin, does accel_step lead force in every completed run so far (here 0.70 vs 0.48 and 0.71 vs 0.42)? Should the lab switch to that criterion for targets whose random controls exceed 0.7?

Does the accel_step margin at step 100 (0.108-0.115) survive regressing distance out of the accel_step target? Distance already has a margin of about 0.65 by step 50, and accel_step depends on 1/r^2, so the early accel_step signal may just be a nonlinear read of distance rather than a separate acceleration representation.

Why is the force margin only 0.068-0.103 in this 4-layer, d_model=64, N=64, 600-step setup, when it reached 0.22-0.24 in earlier runs? Is the difference driven by steps_per_orbit, model size, or training length? A one-factor sweep of steps_per_orbit (64 vs 1000) at fixed architecture would separate these.

On the high_eccentricity eval set, do force and accel_step probes still beat a random-init control evaluated on the same OOD data? Best force R2 drops from about 0.7 to 0.34-0.40, but without an OOD control we cannot tell whether the force representation broke or the R2 ceiling moved.

Does training on eccentricity [0, 0.8] and evaluating on held-out e in [0.5, 0.8] bring the high-e val_mse_ratio back within about 3x of in-distribution (as low_mass_ratio is)? If it does, the 16-18x gap is a coverage limit of the training range, not evidence of a non-physical shortcut.
Is the force-over-accel_step margin ordering in small models (L=2, d=32) a stable property of scale or a seed effect?
Does a symbolic fit to the gravity direction recover an m2 factor (physical force) or an a^3 orbit-scale factor (per-snapshot acceleration) when m2 spans [0.01, 1]?
If training runs the full 3000 steps (not stopping at 2000), do the symbolic fits for the accel_step direction settle on a^3/r^2 in both seeds, or does seed 11's r^-1 form persist?

The force-direction symbolic fit gives (m2 + c)/r, with an r exponent of -1 rather than -2. Is that because the fit is confounded with distance (margin 0.62-0.65 at layers 1-2), and would fitting after regressing distance out of the probe output recover r^-2?

With m2 fixed, force and accel_step differ only by the a^3 orbit-scale factor. Does the accel_step random-control R2 stay at 0.71-0.76 in that setting? If it does, the a^3 factor visible in raw input coordinates is likely what drives accel_step's high control.

Did the E3 runs stop at step 2000 because symbolic probing at every checkpoint used up the 0.2 h budget? If final-only symbolic probing finishes all 3000 steps, should symbolic experiments default to checkpoints = 'final'?

Prediction error on held-out high-e systems matches low-e (val_mse_ratio about 0.019 for both), yet the best force probe R2 falls from 0.73-0.80 to 0.37. Is that because 1/r^2 has heavier tails at pericentre, which lowers linear-probe R2 on high-e data, or because the force representation itself degrades at high e? Probing log(force), and fitting a random-init control on the same eval sets, would tell these apart.

Why did both E4 runs stop at step 2500 of 3000 when they had used only about 0.13 of the 0.2 h budget and ran final-only probing with no symbolic fits? Does training to 3000 steps keep lowering val_mse_ratio (still dropping from 0.034 to 0.018) and change the probe margins?

Seed 13's accel_step fit has denominator m2*r^2 + r, which runs from r^-1 at small m2 to r^-2 at m2 near 1. Is the effective r exponent of the encoded gravity direction actually m2-dependent? Fitting separately on m2 < 0.1 and m2 > 0.5 subsets would test this.

With eccentricity in [0, 0.5], r stays within a narrow band around a, so a^3/r^2, a^2/r and a are nearly collinear. If eccentricity is widened to [0, 0.9], or the symbolic fit is restricted to systems in a narrow band of a so that r is the only thing varying, does the accel_step-direction fit recover r^-2 and a^3, or does r^-1 persist?

With eccentricity widened to [0, 0.9], does the accel_step random-control R2 fall well below its usual 0.71-0.76 (as it fell to 0.35-0.38 with e in [0, 0.8])? If so, the high control at e <= 0.5 comes from r tracking the input-visible orbit scale a, and headroom-normalized margins should be reported for low-e runs.

If r^-1 persists in symbolic fits even when r and a are decorrelated, is the model encoding a velocity-squared-over-r (centripetal-like, v^2/r) quantity rather than GM/r^2? The two coincide for circular orbits and diverge at high eccentricity.

With m2 fixed, force (0.5/r^2) and accel_step (proportional to a^3/r^2) differ only by the a^3 orbit-scale factor, yet accel_step is decoded at 0.92-0.95 versus 0.73-0.75 for force. Is accel_step's advantage just that a^3, which varies widely across systems and is visible in the inputs, dominates its variance? Probing a^3 alone, and probing accel_step after removing each system's mean, would show whether any per-snapshot 1/r^2 structure is left.

With m2 fixed, does a linear probe on 1/r, log(force), or a small MLP probe on force reach R2 of 0.85 or more at layers 1-2? That would tell us whether the force ceiling is a limit of linear readout of a distance-like code (distance R2 0.87-0.89) or a real absence of a 1/r^2 feature.

With e in [0, 0.9], does an MLP probe or a linear probe on log(accel_step) reach R2 >= 0.8 at layer 4, and does a symbolic fit to that probe's output recover r^-2? If yes, the persistent r^-1 is a limit of linear readout. If the fit stays r^-1, the model really does encode a non-1/r^2 quantity.

Linearly decodable accel_step falls from R2 0.92-0.95 (e <= 0.5) to 0.40-0.50 (e <= 0.9), yet val_mse_ratio stays at 0.013. Where does the model's next-step accuracy come from on high-e snapshots? Does probe R2 binned by r/a, or activation patching at layer 4, show it relying on distance (margin 0.51-0.61) plus a learned nonlinearity in later layers instead?

Since r lies in [a(1-e), a(1+e)], a and r exponents are confounded in free-form symbolic fits. If the accel_step probe output is fit as a^p * g(r/a), with p and the shape g fitted separately, does p come out near 1 and g near (r/a)^-2, as a^3/r^2 predicts?

Should symbolic fits only be run when the probe R2 is at least 0.8? All fits here (error 0.55-0.65) come from probe directions with R2 0.35-0.50, so the fitted exponents may reflect probe noise rather than what the model encodes.

Is accel_step's high random-control R2 (0.71-0.76 at e <= 0.5) partly due to per-step acceleration being nearly a linear function of second differences of the input positions? If so, would a probe at a token position whose prior inputs are masked, or a control built from finite differences of the raw inputs, give a fairer baseline for 'learned' acceleration?

Does the training step at which accel_step forms (step 100 at N=64) shift with steps_per_orbit? If structure forms earlier at N=16 and later or never at N=256, formation timing is set by task demand rather than by a fixed stage of optimization.

If the same symbolic-regression pipeline is fit directly to the true accel_step target (a^3/r^2 scaled) on these e in [0, 0.7], m2 fixed systems, does it recover r^-2 with fit error < 0.2? If it also returns r^-1 or a two-term a^2/r form, the persistent r^-1 is caused by the fitting procedure rather than by the model's representation.

Does seed 24, rerun after fixing the dataset-cache rename failure (data.tmp.npz to data.npz, possibly a race when seeds share a dataset), reproduce accel_step R2 >= 0.8 together with an r^-1 symbolic fit? A second seed is needed before the r^-1 result counts as replicated.

Force peaks at layer 4 in seed 16 but at layers 1-2 in seeds 14 and 15. Is the per-layer force R2 profile flat within about 0.03, so the best-layer choice is noise, or does the layer where force is best actually vary from seed to seed?

With m2 fixed, energy = -m2/(2a) depends only on a, and it is decoded at R2 0.91 at layer 1 (margin 0.57). Does a linear probe for a^3 at layer 4 match accel_step's R2 of 0.94? If it does, accel_step decoding is explained by an orbit-scale feature rather than per-snapshot 1/r^2 structure.

Every accel_step symbolic fit at R2 >= 0.8 so far gives r^-1. Should the lab add a probe target for 1/r or a^2/r, so a linear probe can directly compare an r^-1 orbit-scale quantity against accel_step, instead of relying on symbolic regression?

At N=256 the constant-velocity baseline is much stronger, so val_mse_ratio is not comparable across steps_per_orbit. Should formation timing be compared against the step where val_mse_ratio falls to a fixed fraction of its step-0 value, rather than against the step where it falls below 1?

Seed 26's accel_step fit_error (0.2008) sits right at the 0.2 law-recovery threshold. How much does fit_error vary when the symbolic fit is rerun on the same probe output with different subsamples or regressor seeds? If the run-to-run spread is about 0.05 or more, a single fit cannot reliably separate r^-1 from r^-2 near the threshold.

In seeds 24 and 26 the accel_step fits have the form a^2/r - c*a with c about 0.55-0.56, close to the vis-viva quantity (2a^2/r - a)/2, which is proportional to (v*dt)^2/a, the squared per-snapshot displacement divided by orbit scale. Does a linear probe for (v*dt)^2/a, or for a^2*(2/r - 1/a), at layer 4 match or beat accel_step's R2 of 0.83-0.88? If it does, the model's gravity-like direction is a velocity-based centripetal quantity rather than a^3/r^2.

With matched seeds and checkpoints every 10 steps over the first 200 steps, does the step where accel_step first reaches a 0.1 margin differ between N=16, N=64 and N=256 by more than the seed-to-seed spread (here 75 vs 100 at N=16)?

In both N=16 seeds, val_mse_ratio falls to about 0.23 by step 50, before accel_step forms and while force margin is still 0.004. Distance and energy margins are already 0.4-0.7 at that point. Is early next-step accuracy carried by distance and orbit-scale features, with accel_step and force forming only during the later refinement phase (val_mse_ratio 0.06 to 0.006)?

Is the N=256 failure to beat the baseline (val MSE about 3e-7, where the per-step displacement change is tiny) caused by target scale or normalization rather than capacity? If inputs and targets are normalized per step, do N=256 models beat the baseline within 600 steps, and does the accel_step formation step change?

At N=256 the model is 3.1-3.2x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation, yet its accel_step margin (0.19-0.21) matches N=64 models that beat the baseline. Does ablating or patching the layer-3 accel_step direction change val MSE at all? If not, the accel_step margin there is decodable but unused by the prediction.

The patching module ranks heads by force R2 only. Would ranking heads by accel_step R2, the target with the larger headroom-normalized margin, pick different heads with larger patching effects? A code change to patch on accel_step would test this directly.

Probe targets are fixed to force, distance, velocity, energy and accel_step. Several open questions (q-20261011-225319-fc03 on a^3, q-20261011-225358-0609 on a^2/r, q-20261011-231118-3513 on (v*dt)^2/a, q-20261011-224242-6402 on the fitter run against the true target) can't be tested through the config. Should these targets and a fitter-on-ground-truth check be added to the probe suite?

Does the accel_step-before-val_mse_ratio<1 ordering still hold when accel_step formation uses a stricter threshold (margin >= 0.15, or headroom-normalised margin >= 0.5)? Seeds 44 and 45 never reach 0.12, so at 0.15 they would show no formation at all within 300 steps.

In all 3 seeds the force margin spikes at step 10 (0.14-0.24, above the 0.1 bar), then decays to about 0-0.07 by step 60-70 and never recovers. Is this early transient a real, short-lived force-like feature, or an artifact of the near-random step-10 weights (e.g. the control set drawing a lower best-of-3 at that checkpoint)? Re-probing step 10 with fresh controls and 3 more seeds would tell these apart.

Every head patch here raises MSE 17-110x, which suggests cross-system swaps break orbit-scale information in every head. If you mean-ablate each head instead, or patch from a system with matched semi-major axis a, does the top force- or accel_step-scoring head then have at least 3x the effect of the lowest-scoring head?

What is the full distribution of patching effects across all 16 heads, and does per-head effect correlate with per-head force or accel_step R2? Comparing only the top and bottom head cannot tell a specific gravity pathway apart from general fragility.

What fit_error_vs_true_law does the exact vis-viva expression a^2/r - a/2 get against a^3/r^2 on the e in [0, 0.7], m2 = 0.5 data? If it is below 0.2, the law-recovery criterion cannot separate r^-1 from r^-2 on this distribution, and E3 fits need a stricter criterion or a higher eccentricity range.

The constant c in the accel_step fit a*(a/r - c) is 0.55-0.56 at 4 layers / d_model=64 and 0.50-0.54 at 6 layers / d_model=128. Does c converge to exactly 0.5 (vis-viva) as models grow or train longer? Does a linear probe for a^2*(2/r - 1/a) at layer 6 match or beat accel_step's R2 of 0.92-0.93?

If the 6-layer accel_step probe R2 drops below 0.8 at e <= 0.85 while val_mse_ratio stays near 0.01, is the gravity computation then spread nonlinearly across layers, so that linear probes stop being an adequate readout at high eccentricity?
Should formed_at_step require persistence (margin >= required_margin at k consecutive checkpoints)? Single-checkpoint crossings at steps 10-25 (force) produce formation steps that later disappear.

The accel_step margin rises smoothly at N=256 and levels off at 0.15-0.18. At the 0.1 bar, formation falls at steps 100-120, but at 0.15 it spans steps 150-240. With matched seeds and best-of-5 controls at N=64 and N=256, does the ordering of formation steps across steps_per_orbit depend on the threshold? Would comparing the step where each run reaches half its own final margin give a threshold-free measure of timing?

At N=256, accel_step forms (step 100-120) while val_mse_ratio is still about 87-98 and never falls below 11. Is the accel_step margin driven by the training data, or by the gradient early in training regardless of task difficulty? Would a model trained on shuffled-time sequences (no dynamics to learn) still develop a 0.1 accel_step margin at about step 100?

Seed 52's accel_step fit is a^3/r^2 with fit_error_vs_true_law 0.068, under the 0.2 threshold, yet law_recovered is false. Which criterion fails: a probe-R2 gate, the coefficient, or something else? Is that criterion documented and applied the same way across all earlier E3 runs?

Widening eccentricity from [0, 0.5] to [0, 0.85] cut the accel_step random-control R2 from 0.71-0.76 to 0.29-0.30, while the trained-model margin rose to about 0.41. Is high eccentricity a cleaner test of learned acceleration, because the orbit-scale a^3 factor no longer dominates accel_step variance? Does the control R2 fall steadily as the eccentricity ceiling rises?

In all 3 N=64 seeds, the trained model's force R2 at layer 4 rises from about 0.37-0.47 to 0.61-0.64 by step 10, then falls back to about 0.43-0.46 by step 40-50, measured against fixed controls. Distance and energy first cross the bar at steps 10-15. Is the step-10 force direction just a nonlinear read of distance or 1/r that later gets overwritten? Does it survive regressing distance out of the force target, and what is its cosine similarity to the later accel_step probe direction?

At N=64 the accel_step margin levels off at 0.13-0.17 because the controls sit at 0.72-0.77. Should E5 formation timing use a headroom-normalized margin or a fraction of each run's own final margin, rather than fixed raw thresholds of 0.1 or 0.15? Those measures give formation steps 50-130, all before val_mse_ratio < 1, while the raw 0.15 bar is never reached in 2 of 3 seeds.

If longer training lifts the e <= 0.85 accel_step probe R2 above 0.8, does probe R2 track val_mse_ratio across checkpoints? That would say whether linear decodability of accel_step at high eccentricity is a byproduct of convergence or a separate representational change.

In all N=16 seeds the distance margin levels off at about 0.54-0.67 by steps 25-30, and accel_step rises steadily from step 30 to step 90 after that. Is accel_step formation downstream of distance formation? For example, does the accel_step rise survive regressing distance out of the target at steps 30-90, and does delaying distance formation also delay accel_step?

accel_step formation is nearly the same at N=16 (steps 75-90) and N=64 (steps 85-90), even though the two baselines and loss scales differ a lot. Does formation instead line up with a fixed training-step window, or with a fixed fraction of step-0 val MSE? At N=16 it happens at val_mse_ratio 0.08-0.10, about 2% of the step-0 value. Comparing the same fraction at N=64 and N=256 would tell these apart.

Seed 54's accel_step fit, a^2/(r+0.17)^2, is a softened r^-2 law, which suggests the probe direction misses the pericentre tail. Binned by r/a, does the layer-6 accel_step probe's R2 or residual fall off sharply for r/a < 0.4? Would probing log(accel_step) remove that loss?

With probes at every 500-step checkpoint for the 6-layer d_model=128 model at e <= 0.85, does accel_step R2 at layer 6 level off near 0.70 by step 1500-2000 while val_mse_ratio keeps falling from 0.05 to 0.0035? A plateau in the same seed would show that linear decodability of accel_step has decoupled from prediction quality at high eccentricity.

With matched seeds and identical 10-step checkpoint spacing, is the N=64 vs N=256 difference in accel_step formation step larger than the within-N seed spread of about 10 steps? If N=256 is consistently later, does the delay scale with log(N) or with the shrinking per-step acceleration (2*pi/N)^2?

accel_step forms at a val_mse_ratio of 2.0-2.6 at N=64, about 2.6-3.1% of each run's step-0 value, compared with about 2% at N=16. In the paired N=256 arm, does formation also happen at about 2-3% of step-0 val MSE, even though N=256 never beats the baseline? That would tie formation to relative loss reduction rather than to a fixed training step.

With the same data and best-of-5 controls, the accel_step control R2 differs across seeds by about 0.06 (0.709-0.769), while the within-run control_spread is only 0.010-0.019. Does the control seed or probe split differ by run seed? Would a control pool shared across all seeds, or a control_spread taken across run seeds, give a fairer required_margin for comparing formation steps across N?

Between steps 2000 and 4000, val_mse_ratio falls 5-7x while linear accel_step R2 gains only about 0.02. Is that late MSE gain concentrated on pericentre snapshots (r/a < 0.4)? Per-checkpoint val MSE and accel_step probe residual, binned by r/a, would show whether late training refines exactly the high-acceleration region that the linear probe fails to read.

At e <= 0.85, accel_step's best layer stays fixed at layer 6 from step 500 on, while force's best layer drifts across layers 1-6 (seed 56: 1 to 2 to 6 to 3; seed 57: 2 to 5 to 6). Is the force per-layer profile flat within about 0.02 at these checkpoints, so that force is only a weaker shadow of the layer-6 accel_step direction? What is the cosine similarity between the force and accel_step probe directions at layer 6?

Across all completed E5 runs, does the step where accel_step first crosses the raw 0.1 margin correlate inversely with that run's final margin, or with its control R2? Here, seed 57 has control 0.778 and final margin 0.118 and forms at step 160, while seeds 56 and 58 have controls 0.68-0.72 and final margins of about 0.17 and form at steps 100-120. A strong correlation would mean raw-threshold formation steps mostly measure the ceiling, not timing.

The early force transient (margin 0.12-0.19 at steps 10-30, fading to about 0 by step 80-110) looks the same at N=256 as the one reported at N=64, even though N=256 never beats the constant-velocity baseline. Is this transient independent of steps_per_orbit and of task success? Would it also appear in a model trained on shuffled-time sequences?

Joining the matched seeds 56-58 at e <= 0.5 on the 0.1 bar (formed_at_step values), N=256 minus N=64 is +20 (seed 56: 100 vs 80), +70 (seed 57: 160 vs 90) and +30 (seed 58: 120 vs 90). On that measure all three are >= 20 steps later. What are the N=64 half-final-margin formation steps for seeds 56-58? They are needed to finish the paired comparison that f-20261012-030313-4d1f left open.

Why does probes_final.formed_at_step lag the per-checkpoint trajectory by one checkpoint in at least two runs (seed 51 at N=256: trajectory 110, formed_at_step 120; seed 48 at N=16: trajectory 70, formed_at_step 75)? Is it an off-by-one, or an undocumented persistence window? Until this is resolved, every E5 formation step should be read from the trajectory, and earlier findings that quote formed_at_step (including f-20261012-030203-1224 and f-20261012-030313-4d1f) should be re-checked against their trajectories.

At e <= 0.85 the accel_step margin rises to 0.26-0.29 only because controls fall to 0.25-0.33, while raw R2 stays at 0.51-0.59. With m2 range and seeds held fixed, does raw accel_step R2 rise toward 0.8 with longer training (val_mse_ratio is still falling at 0.13), or is linear decodability of accel_step capped near 0.6 at high eccentricity?

At e <= 0.85 and N=64, accel_step forms at steps 60-70 when val_mse_ratio is about 8-10% of its step-0 value. At e <= 0.5 the same N formed at steps 85-90 and about 2-3%. Does the paired N=256 e <= 0.85 arm (seeds 59-61) also form within a similar training-step window? If so, formation timing tracks training steps rather than relative loss reduction, across both N and eccentricity.

At N=256 and e <= 0.85, distance crosses its bar at steps 20-40 and accel_step at 60-70 in all 3 seeds, a consistent 20-40 step lag. Does the same lag appear at N=64 for seeds 59-61? Is the step where distance forms predictive of the step where accel_step forms, run by run?

accel_step forms at steps 60-70 whatever the steps_per_orbit (64 vs 256), eccentricity range, or task success (N=256 never beats the baseline). Is that window set by the optimizer rather than the data? If lr is halved or batch_size doubled at fixed N=64, e <= 0.85, does the formation step move in proportion to the change (about 2x later), or stay near step 60-70?

Does the N=256 vs N=64 formation delay depend on eccentricity? At e<=0.5 (seeds 56-58) N=256 was 10-70 steps later; at e<=0.85 (seeds 59-61) it was within 10 steps. Is the delay tied to the high accel_step control R2 (0.71-0.78) at low e?

Seed 62 has the smallest final accel_step margin (0.144) and the earliest half-final step (60), while seed 63 has 0.160 and reaches half-final at step 90. Across all completed E5 runs, does the half-final-margin step correlate with the run's final margin? If it does, the measure picks up plateau height as well as timing, and a threshold on headroom-normalized margin may be a better way to compare timing.

At N=64, distance forms 70-90 steps before accel_step at e <= 0.5 (steps 10-20 vs 90-100) but only 20-40 steps before it at e <= 0.85. Is the distance-to-accel_step lag set by how high the accel_step random control is (0.72-0.75 here vs 0.25-0.33 at high e), rather than by when the model actually starts computing acceleration?

Pooling matched seeds 56-64 at e <= 0.5 and reading every N=64 and N=256 formation step from the trajectories, is the mean N=256 minus N=64 delay on the 0.1 bar and the half-final measure different from 0 by more than one checkpoint (10 steps)? Seeds 56-58 gave +20/+70/+30, but seeds 62-64 gave only 0-20.

At N=256, accel_step forms when val_mse_ratio is 83-95, which is 5.9-7.3% of the step-0 value, compared with the 2-3% reported at N=64. Since a relative-loss threshold does not line up across N, does formation instead line up with a fixed training step (about 90-110 at e <= 0.5 for both N)?

Halving lr delayed formation by only 10-30 steps. Does a dose-response sweep (lr 0.00025, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.002) at N=64, e <= 0.85, seeds 59-61 show formation step scaling as a weak power of 1/lr? That would say whether the window is mostly set by update count (for example warmup or Adam moment statistics) rather than by distance travelled in parameter space.

At lr=0.0005, accel_step crosses the 0.1 bar when val_mse_ratio is 1.8-2.9. That is close to the 2.0-2.6 reported at N=64, e <= 0.5, lr=0.001, but it is 6-11% of step-0 rather than 2-3%. Across lr values and eccentricity ranges at N=64, is formation better predicted by an absolute val_mse_ratio of about 2-3 than by training step or by fraction of step-0 loss?

The analysis step reported that it 'could not read' the N=64 finding file for seeds 62-64, so it used N=64 values quoted in open-question summaries instead of the run trajectories. Is this a pipeline read failure (path, timing, or file-lock race like the earlier data.tmp.npz rename bug)? Should paired-arm analyses join the per-checkpoint trajectories straight from the run records rather than from other findings?
